Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

DesignComplexSurvival 0.3.0

  • Stage 3 of the development plan: further models of switching and censoring, switching that starts at a calendar time, and recycling of the level between PFS and OS. With the default values of the new arguments the results are unchanged: the outputs of inst/reproduce/ and inst/validation/ of version 0.2.2 are reproduced without any numerical difference.
  • ms_model() gains switch_clock: with "switch", the death hazard after a switch is a function of the time since the switch instead of the post-progression clock ("same", the default).
  • ms_model() gains switch_af, an accelerated failure time effect of the switch: the remaining time after the switch is the remaining time without switch divided by switch_af (the rank preserving structural failure time model of Robins and Tsiatis 1991).
  • ms_model() gains switching before progression: switch_pre (hazard of switching while progression-free), prog_switch and death_switch_pre (hazards of progression and death after such a switch). After a later progression these patients die with the hazard death_switch (with switch_af, switch_af * death_prog). ms_prob() then adds the column progression_free_switched.
  • ms_scenario() gains pfs_switch: PFS is followed up to progression or death ("event", the default) or censored at a switch before progression ("censor").
  • ms_model() gains dropout_pfs, a censoring of PFS only (for example the end of tumour assessments). The PFS dropouts of ms_events() include it and, with pfs_switch = "censor", the censoring at a switch.
  • ms_scenario() gains switch_start, a calendar time before which nobody switches (for example when switching is allowed only after an interim analysis). The distribution of OS then depends on the entry time, and the moments and covariances of the OS statistic integrate over the entry time. Under the null hypothesis the score no longer has independent increments, and the correlations between the looks come from the per-patient influence functions. The OS statistic alone with mean = "direct" is covered, at calendar times or at looks driven by OS events; PFS is not affected. Two endpoints together give an error.
  • ms_test() gains transition for mtp = "bonferroni": the level of a rejected hypothesis is passed on to the other (graphical procedure of Maurer and Bretz 2013, Algorithm 1), and gs_prob_mtp() gains upper_recycled. The bounds after recycling are checked not to exceed the bounds at the initial level at every look. With recycling, the table of ms_power() gains the columns z_upper_recycled and p_upper_recycled.
  • Reproduction scripts added for Maurer and Bretz (2013) and Torres-Saavedra et al. (2026) (inst/reproduce/).
  • Validation: Python simulations of the new options (switch clock and accelerated failure time effect; switching before progression and censoring of PFS only, with PFS and OS together; switching from a calendar time), the Bonferroni procedure with recycling in the simulations of PFS and OS together, and a comparison of the rejection probabilities with the decisions of lrstat::fseqbon() and of the bounds with lrstat::getBound() (inst/validation/).

DesignComplexSurvival 0.2.2

  • Bug fix: rectangle probabilities of nine or more coordinates with two finite limits for some coordinate (designs with futility bounds and nine or more looks of an endpoint) were wrong with the Miwa algorithm of mvtnorm, which leaves out the terms of nine or more coordinates of the inclusion-exclusion over the limits (errors of 7.5e-4 with nine and 6.9e-3 with ten coordinates under the correlation of independent increments, so also with the default variance = "null"). They now use the Genz-Bretz algorithm with a fixed seed. Rectangles with one-sided limits only (no futility bounds) and designs with at most eight looks per endpoint are unchanged.

DesignComplexSurvival 0.2.1

  • Bug fix: with variance = "alternative" or "studentized" and four or more looks of an endpoint, the stopping probabilities, the power, the futility bounds by beta spending and the familywise error rates under null_scenarios were computed with the Miwa algorithm, which is inaccurate for covariance matrices that are not those of statistics with independent increments (errors of about 1e-3 with four looks and above 0.1 with six or more looks, found by comparison with exact values). Rectangle probabilities of four or more coordinates with such a covariance matrix now use the Genz-Bretz algorithm with a fixed seed, in gs_prob(), gs_bounds() and gs_prob_mtp() as well. The default variance = "null", the efficacy bounds, the type I error and designs with at most three looks per endpoint are unchanged.
  • The option for the absolute error tolerance of the Genz-Bretz algorithm is renamed DesignComplexSurvival.genz_abseps (formerly DesignComplexSurvival.mtp_abseps); the default remains 1e-5.
  • With binding futility bounds, a futility bound that reaches the efficacy bound at an interim look stops every trial there, so that the efficacy bounds of the later looks cannot be computed; the error message now names that look.

DesignComplexSurvival 0.2.0

  • Stage 2 of the development plan: designs that test progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) together.
  • ms_test() gains mtp ("none", "bonferroni" or "fixed_sequence"), weights and hierarchical ("overall" or "stagewise", procedures (b) and (a) of Glimm et al. 2010), added after the existing arguments. endpoints may name both endpoints in the order of testing, and sf_eff and param_eff may differ between them. Each endpoint has its own efficacy bounds; futility bounds are placed on the first endpoint.
  • ms_looks() accepts one trigger per look ("os", "pfs" or "calendar") and, through test, the endpoints tested at each look.
  • ms_power() returns, for two endpoints, the power of each endpoint, the probability of rejecting both and at least one hypothesis, and the familywise error rate under the global null hypothesis and under user-given partial null scenarios (null_scenarios). events takes the final numbers of events named by endpoint, for example c(pfs = 300, os = 220).
  • ms_size() gains target ("first", "each", "both" or "any") and null_scenarios; with looks driven by the events of both endpoints, solve_for = "events" rounds up the final numbers of events of both.
  • lr_cov() returns the joint distribution of the PFS and OS statistics (endpoint = c("pfs", "os")). Under the null hypothesis their covariance is that of Danzer et al. (2025, Theorem 1).
  • New option variance = "studentized" in lr_moments(), lr_cov() and ms_test(): the asymptotic covariance of the standardized statistic itself, including the variability of the variance estimator and, through trigger, of the analysis times driven by observed numbers of events. The default remains variance = "null", and the results of the existing options are unchanged.
  • New function gs_prob_mtp(): rejection probabilities of the two hypotheses under the Bonferroni and fixed-sequence procedures. Rectangles of four or more coordinates over both endpoints use the Genz-Bretz algorithm with a fixed seed (absolute error set by options(DesignComplexSurvival.mtp_abseps = ...), default 1e-5); the other probabilities use the Miwa algorithm as before. mvtnorm (>= 1.2-0) is now required.
  • print(), summary() and as.data.frame() methods handle two endpoints.
  • Reproduction scripts added for Glimm et al. (2010), Tamhane et al. (2010), Sugimoto et al. (2017) and Erdmann et al. (2025) (inst/reproduce/).
  • Validation: a Python simulation of PFS and OS analysed together in four scenarios, with designs of two endpoints, and the covariance estimator of Danzer et al. (2025) applied to large simulated trials under the null hypothesis (inst/validation/). The Python simulation of single endpoints now counts the event at an event-driven analysis time in every trial.

DesignComplexSurvival 0.1.0

  • First version (stage 1 of the development plan): designs that test one endpoint, progression-free survival (PFS) or overall survival (OS).
  • Model: a four-state model per group (progression-free, progressed, switched, dead) with piecewise constant intensities, immediate switching at progression and switching after progression, and a choice of the clock of the post-progression intensities (clock = "reset" or "forward") (ms_model(), ms_fleischer()); piecewise uniform accrual by rates or by proportions (ms_accrual()); piecewise exponential dropout by group.
  • Endpoint distributions and state occupation probabilities (ms_surv(), ms_prob()), expected events and dropouts over calendar time (ms_events(), ms_event_time()).
  • Mean, variance and covariance of the log-rank statistic over calendar time (lr_moments(), lr_cov()), with the mean by the direct formula or the Schoenfeld approximation and the covariance with unit variances or under the alternative (Luo et al. 2019).
  • Group sequential designs: alpha spending for efficacy; no futility, fixed futility bounds (Z or hazard ratio scale) or beta spending; binding or non-binding futility (gs_spend(), gs_bounds(), gs_prob()).
  • Power and type I error (ms_power()) and the number of events, sample size, accrual duration or follow-up for a target power (ms_size()), with event-driven or calendar-driven looks (ms_looks(), ms_test()).
  • Tests compare the results with an independent Python implementation (inst/validation/python/) and, when installed, with gsDesign, gsDesign2, rpact and lrstat.
  • Scripts that reproduce published sample sizes, numbers of events, analysis times, bounds and powers (inst/reproduce/) and compare the package with patient-level simulations (FastSurvival and Python) and with PWEALL (inst/validation/). Each folder writes its judgements to results/summary.csv and results/summary.md.
